learningObjective: Correctly define TF32 and its relationship to FP32.
stem: TF32 (TensorFloat-32) is a numerical format used by NVIDIA Tensor Cores starting with Ampere. Which best describes TF32?

options.text: TF32 is a 24-bit format used by CPU vector units for machine-learning workloads; it is unrelated to GPU Tensor Cores.
TF32 is a 32-bit format equivalent to FP32; the name is a marketing rebrand with no numerical difference.
TF32 is a 16-bit format identical to BF16; the '32' refers to the accumulator width.

TF32 is a 19-bit internal Tensor Core input format: 1 sign, 8 exponent (FP32 range), 10 mantissa (FP16 precision). Storage remains FP32; only the Tensor Core multiplier truncates mantissa on input. Accumulation is FP32.

explanation: TF32 is a Tensor Core input format: 8-bit exponent (FP32 dynamic range) with 10-bit mantissa (FP16 precision), totaling 19 bits internally. Storage in memory remains FP32; the truncation happens as inputs enter the Tensor Core multiplier. The accumulator stays FP32. This gives roughly 8-16× the compute throughput of pure FP32 while preserving FP32 range for training. TF32 is the default matmul mode for FP32 tensors on Ampere+ when `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True`. Options B, C, D misrepresent the format.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: TF32 is a GPU Tensor Core format.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: TF32 has different mantissa precision from FP32.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: TF32 is not identical to BF16 (different mantissa width).

assumptions: The reader is on Ampere or newer NVIDIA GPUs.
nonImplications: Does not imply TF32 matches FP32 accuracy bit-for-bit — the mantissa truncation is observable in numerical tests.
Does not imply TF32 is used automatically for all FP32 tensors — a flag controls it in PyTorch and other frameworks.
